memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Do not hold back offerings from your granaries or your vats. You must give me the firstborn of your sons. Do the same with your cattle and your sheep. Let them stay with their mothers for seven days, but give them to me on the eighth day." - Exodus 22:29-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God tells His people not to hold back, but to give Him the first and the best — the firstfruits of the harvest, the firstborn of the flock. This was Israel's way of declaring a profound truth: everything belongs to God, and He deserves our first and finest, not our leftovers. Giving Him the first was an act of trust, saying, "I believe You will provide the rest."

The order matters. God asks for the first, not the leftovers, because what we give first reveals what holds first place in our hearts. It is easy to give God our spare moments, our spare change, our leftover energy. But He invites us to something higher — to put Him first in our time, our resources, and our devotion, trusting that a life which honours Him first will not lack what it needs (Matt 6:33).

This principle finds its fullest meaning in Christ. Jesus is called the firstborn over all creation and the firstfruits of those raised from the dead (Col 1:15; 1 Cor 15:20). And God did not hold back His own firstborn Son but gave Him freely for us. In light of such generous love, how could we hold back from Him? Giving God our first is simply our grateful response to the God who gave us His best.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I giving God my first and best, or merely my leftovers?
What would it look like to put God first in my time and resources this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You did not hold back Your own Son but gave Him freely for me. Teach me to give You my first and best in glad response, trusting You to provide all I need. Amen.
